options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Albert Einstein, in 1905: cities expand at the speed of light
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: George Zipf, in 1949: the population of the nth ranked city is 1/n times the population of the largest city
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Urban Hierarchy Theories.

options.text: Adam Smith, in 1776: city populations are determined by the invisible hand
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Urban Hierarchy Theories (India: People and Economy - Population & Settlements):
The Rank-Size Rule was popularized by George Zipf in 1949, stating that the population of the nth ranked city will be 1/n of the population of the largest city in the country (Pn = P1 / n).
Hence Option A is correct.

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.

questionText: What are the major environmental consequences of rapid, unplanned rural-to-urban migration in Indian megacities?

options.text: The complete elimination of municipal solid waste
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Instant conversion of city streets into pristine national parks
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Overcrowding in cities, proliferation of unhygienic slums, severe strain on civic infrastructure, water depletion, and untreated sewage discharge
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

options.text: Reduction in urban air pollution to absolute zero
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Unchecked rural-urban migration places acute pressure on urban infrastructure, causing housing deficits, growth of unauthorized slums, water shortages, traffic congestion, and solid waste crises in metropolitan cities.
Hence Option C is correct.
Hence, option (C) is correct.

questionText:
Match List I (Rural Settlement Pattern) with List II (Terrain / Spatial Feature):

List I:
(A) Linear Pattern
(B) Circular Pattern
(C) Star-like Pattern
(D) Rectangular Pattern

List II:
(I) Around a central lake, pond, or village common pasture
(II) Along a road, railway line, river levee, or canal embankment
(III) Flat fertile plains with roads intersecting at right angles
(IV) Convergence of multiple roads with houses radiating outward

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.

options.text: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Linear pattern develops along roads/rivers (II); Circular pattern develops around lakes/ponds (I); Star-like develops along converging roads (IV); Rectangular develops in flat plains (III).
Hence Option C is correct.
Hence, option (B) is the correct match.

questionText: According to the Census of India, what constitutes a 'Statutory Town'?

options.text: Places with a municipality, corporation, cantonment board, or notified town area committee
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Urban Definitions.

options.text: Any forest clearing where nomadic herders pitch tents for two nights
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Any village that contains more than 10 sheep
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Any uninhabited mountain valley
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for India: People and Economy - Population & Settlements (Urban Definitions):
Places with a municipality, corporation, cantonment board, or notified town area committee

Detailed Context:
According to the Census of India, a statutory town is any place with a municipality, municipal corporation, cantonment board, or notified town area committee.
Hence Option D is correct.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.
